comment: AC-13 (#857). The ai-review test case titles as they stood at baseCommit, immediately before #853/#856/#857, with deliberate renames applied in place and recorded in `renames` below. test/ai-review-surface-census.test.ts asserts every one is STILL present and that the surface has grown. A case renamed on purpose edits its entry here in the same commit and adds a `renames` row saying why; a case deleted has to say why. Regenerating the whole list from HEAD makes this green and makes it evidence about nothing.

renames.from: AC-4: it WARNS — the exit code is unmoved, in both directions
renames.to: AC-4 (#866), the PAIR: the runtime's own write is exit 0, anything else refuses
renames.why: The case asserted the outside-the-checkout reading warns rather than refuses, and said why: the noise floor had never been measured. #866 measured it over two runs — 25 paths, all runtime state, none reviewer output — so the posture moved and the case moved with it. It keeps both directions, which is what made it protection: the runtime's own write is still exit 0.

renames.from: AC-7: model pin — no bare opus, sonnet or haiku alias reaches the action
renames.to: AC-7: model pin — no bare family alias reaches the action
renames.why: The title ENUMERATED the three families the case's own local `/(opus|sonnet|haiku)/i` knew. #685 deleted that second decider and delegated to `modelAliasViolations`, whose `MODEL_FAMILY_ALIASES` has carried `fable` since it was written — so the old title named a narrower set than the case now checks, and leaving it would have read as a promise the case no longer makes. The subject, the document under test and the assertion direction are unchanged; the case got WIDER, not weaker, and `AC-7: model pin — planting an alias turns the detector red` now plants every declared family rather than only `opus`.

renames.from: baseline THEN restore — the defect verbatim — is RED and names the file
renames.to: baseline THEN restore — the defect verbatim — is named as a RESTORE, not as the reviewer
renames.why: The case asserted the drift step REFUSES a restore that landed after the baseline, as the behavioural control proving #836's reorder is load-bearing. #989 made the drift step classify a changed path in the twice-restored set BY CONTENT against the base branch, and the bytes a late restore leaves ARE the base's — so it is now acquitted, which is the correct answer: the reviewer did not write them, and saying it did is the misattribution #824 and #851 each measured at length. The order is still asserted, directly and over both the generated and the committed workflow, by the `orders restore before baseline` case in the same file; this one was a behavioural PROXY for that property and has stopped tracking it, and a proxy that passes for the wrong reason is worse than no proxy. The subject and the document under test are unchanged and the case did not get weaker: it now requires the classification to fire, to name the file, and to not call it a reviewer write, so DELETING the classification turns it red in the other direction. AC-M4b in test/ai-review-moving-base.test.ts asserts the same acquittal from the other side, so the two cannot drift apart silently.

renames.from: AC-9: a successful review warns that its findings are not enforced
renames.to: AC-9b: a BLOCKED reading fails the job — #675's second half
renames.why: The case asserted the SHIPPED posture of the day: a completed review's payload is warned about and the check goes green, because no step ran the reader. #1013 made the step run it, so the posture the case protected no longer exists — a payload carrying a blocking finding now exits non-zero, which is the state #675 AC-4 asked for and this case was the record of NOT having. The subject is unchanged (a completed review, a payload on disk, what the job does with it) and the case got STRONGER: it now requires the exit code to move, so deleting the adjudication turns it red, where before deleting the warning turned it red. The warn-and-pass direction did not vanish with it — AC-9c asserts it for the one state where it is still correct, an adjudicator that could not run, and AC-9a asserts a clean reading still passes, so the refusal is not unconditional.

renames.from: AC-9: a consumer who required a review is refused an unenforced one
renames.to: AC-9d: a consumer who required a review is refused an unadjudicated one
renames.why: Same property, narrower subject. RUNGATE_REQUIRE_AI_REVIEW had to cover "a payload nobody reads" because nothing in the job read one; after #1013 something does, so what remains for it to cover is an adjudicator that could not run. The assertion direction, the variable and the exit code are unchanged; the input moved from "a payload, always" to "a payload and a bunx that produced no reading".

renames.from: AC-9: the two completed/not-completed states say different things
renames.to: AC-9f: the two completed/not-completed states say different things
renames.why: Renumbered only, for the a-f ordering #1013 gave the block. The pair, the one varied reading and both assertions are unchanged apart from what the two sentences are compared on: the old form looked for "#675" in the completed sentence, which #1013 removed from it, so it looks for the adjudicator package name the sentence now carries.

renames.from: AC-9d: a consumer who required a review is refused an unadjudicated one
renames.to: AC-9d: THE PAIR — no credential warns, an unread payload does not
renames.why: #1013 shipped this case asserting that RUNGATE_REQUIRE_AI_REVIEW covers a payload nothing adjudicated — warn by default, refuse only on opt-in. The team lead's review of #1076 caught that as a FAIL-OPEN: a payload exists, so a review WAS attempted and its result is on disk, and 'nobody read it' is then indistinguishable from 'adjudicated clean' on a required check. The flag is for a tree with no credential, where nothing was attempted at all. So the state the old case was about no longer exists — it refuses unconditionally now — and the replacement is the PAIR that keeps the two apart: no credential still warns and exits 0, an unread payload refuses, and the third run shows the flag does not change the second. The case got STRONGER: it now fails if the refusal stops firing AND if the no-credential path starts firing, where the old one only checked the opt-in path. AC-9c asserts the refusal directly and AC-9e runs the mutant that would undo it.
